verified.title: The 0.635 'perfect wording' figure only holds for v7's own menu. It is not a ceiling for any English reader, and other wordings that already exist pass 0.686
verified.evidence: I reproduced the claim exactly. In memory, v4 on questions(docs, dsids, True, 32, wordings={k:[v[0][0]]}) gives 0.635 (link 0.45, combine 0.955, compare 0.5). The oracle set lines up with the test set: all 50 ids, expected answers, gold_docs and pieces match, and in-memory answering reproduces all 50 published v4 and v7 answers (0 mismatches). The claim only tries the first training wording, which is what menu() uses at reader.py:34 (`w = train[0]`). With the same v4 weights on the same 50 questions: (a) taking training wording #2 for action items (8/8 instead of 7/8) and compare (5/8 instead of 4/8), and wording #1 elsewhere, gives 0.692. (b) The earlier fixed BLIND writer-2 set, used unchanged, gives 0.718. (c) issue_pr_author scores 0/5 under all three training wordings but 3/5 under T held-out #2 ('Who is the author of the GitHub pull request tied to {k}?'), RETEST #1 and NEW_WORDS #2; the plan becomes referenced_by [github] → author. (d) The best fixed wording per kind across the 13 wording lists in factbank_multi.py gives 0.783. Even with compare held at chance (0.5) it is link 0.60 + combine 1.00 → 0.700.
verified.impact: Rule 1 stays 'not met'. But the conclusion drawn from it, that no English reader in front of v4 could reach 0.686 and so the reader is not the bottleneck, does not follow. What the data supports is: 'with v7's menu, a perfect rewriter scores 0.635.' Choosing the first training wording for the menu costs about 0.06 by itself. The counter-examples beat 0.686 by only 1 to 3 questions, and some of those answers are right by coincidence (see the compare and hub findings). So the honest statement is 'a ceiling cannot be shown either way', not 'impossible'.

verdict.reason:
I reran the reviewer's numbers in memory with read-only Python (sqlite opened mode=ro, no files written) and every one of them reproduces.

Baseline checks:
- Regenerating mdllm's questions with questions(docs, dsids, True, 32, wordings=BLIND2) reproduces questions.jsonl exactly.
- v4 answered in memory gives 0 mismatches against factbank_v4.jsonl and scores 0.586.
- The oracle set built with {k: [v[0][0]]} lines up with the published 50 questions on ids, expected answers, gold_docs and pieces. On it v4 scores 0.635 (link 0.45, combine 0.955, compare 0.5).
- That oracle is only the target of reader.py:34 (`w = train[0]`), the first training wording that menu() puts in front of the model.

Fixed wording lists, same v4 weights, same 50 questions:
- train#2 0.575, train#3 0.602, held#2 0.621, BLIND2 writer-1 0.650.
- BLIND writer-2 0.718 (link 0.45, combine 0.955, compare 0.75), used unchanged.
- Mix (a), training wording #2 for action items and compare and #1 elsewhere: 0.692.
- Best wording per kind and field across the 13 lists: 0.783. Taking the best wording separately for each question also gives 0.783.

Per kind:
- issue_pr_author is 0/5 under all three training wordings.
- It is 3/5 under T held-out #2, RETEST #1 and NEW_WORDS #2.
- In 2 of those 3 (016, 038) the plan is the correct `referenced_by [github] → author`. The third (021) goes via a sub_issues detour.

So "no English reader in front of v4 could reach 0.686" does not follow. The 0.635 is what a reader scores when it rewrites exactly to v7's menu. It is not a ceiling over English rewrites. Under the pre-registered measure, wordings that already exist score 0.69 to 0.78.

Caveat, which supports the reviewer's softer wording rather than refuting it:
- The margins are 1 to 3 questions, and several of them are right by coincidence.
- The compare plans clearly wander. For example compare_two-049 under BLIND writer-2 uses "POC weekly network readiness & upgrade playbook → redwood_attendees → assignee_of → created_at → earliest".
- With compare held at 0.5, BLIND writer-2 falls to 0.635 and mix (a) to 0.650.
- Training wording #1 everywhere plus T held-out #2 for issue_pr_author gives 0.685, just under the bar. Adding training wording #2 for action items gives 0.700.

The honest statement is: "with v7's menu, a perfect rewriter scores 0.635; whether any reader could reach 0.686 cannot be shown either way." The impossibility claim is overstated, so the finding is real. It concerns how the result is interpreted, not any computed number.
verdict.corrected_impact:
No published number or rule decision changes:
- Test set: v4 0.586, v7 0.573, v8 0.601.
- Training: v4 0.927, v7 0.966, v8 0.986.
- Changed copy: v7 0.558, v8 0.601.
- Rules 1-3 not met, 4-5 met. Rule 1 stays not met because v7 is 0.573, below 0.686.

What has to change is the interpretive sentence. It should read: "re-asked in v7's menu wording (first training wording, reader.py:34), v4 scores 0.635, so a perfect rewriter onto this menu could not meet rule 1."

It should not say that no English reader could. Pre-existing wordings reach:
- 0.692: training wording #2 for action items and compare.
- 0.718: BLIND writer-2 used unchanged.
- 0.783: best wording per kind across the 13 lists.

These margins rest on 1 to 3 questions, partly coincidental:
- With compare fixed at 0.5 the figures are 0.650, 0.635 and 0.700.
- Training wording #1 plus a swap for issue_pr_author alone gives 0.685.

So whether any reader could reach 0.686 cannot be settled either way. The menu choice costs between about 0 and 0.06, depending on whether the compare answers count.

verified.title: The claim that no English reader in front of v4 could reach 0.686 only holds for v7's menu (the first training wording). Using training wording 2 for two kinds gives 0.692
verified.evidence: The 0.635 itself reproduces. questions(docs, dsids, True, 32, wordings={k:[v[0][0]]}) gives the same 50 questions as mdllm/questions.jsonl, matching position by position on id, kind, field, expected and pieces. A 1-option and a 2-option rng.choice use the same random words, so seed 32 does not drift. Rebuilding the BLIND2 set is byte-identical, and v4 re-answered in memory against a read-only bank scores mean 0.635 (link 0.45, combine 0.955, compare 0.5). But menu() picks only train[0], and v4 was trained on all three training wordings. The same construction with each wording gives: wording 1 0.635, wording 2 0.575, wording 3 0.602. Choosing one fixed wording per (kind, field) gives 0.692: wording 2 for action_owner_issues (8/8 vs 7/8) and for compare_two (5/8 vs 4/8), wording 1 for the rest; link 0.45, combine 1.0, compare 0.625. Picking the best of the 3 wordings per question also gives 0.692. With v7's own menu plus a perfect choice of keeping the original question, the ceiling is 0.650 (only action_owner_issues-030 is right on the original and wrong on the standard wording). The cap does not come from English. The 48 training questions contain no pr_issue due_date question (kind_assoc targets are key 32, person 9, count 8, other 10; never 'date'). So pr_issue-due_date (4 questions) and issue_pr_author (5) score 0 under every one of the 5 T wordings. For example, 'When is the Linear issue linked from PR #28544 due?' picks the assignee plan: kind_assoc is 0.406 for it and 0.0 for the due_date plan, even though the due_date plan returns the right 2026-03-10.
verified.impact: No published number or rule verdict changes. The conclusion as worded is too strong. What is supported: a perfect reader into v7's frozen menu caps v4 at 0.635 to 0.650, below 0.686. A reader free to choose any training wording could just reach 0.692. That choice was made after seeing the test set and the margin is 0.006. About 9 of the 20 link questions are out of reach because of what the training set covers, not because of English.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. Every number reproduces exactly. I ran v4 again in memory, with sqlite opened in mode=ro and no files written.
- The BLIND2 rebuild, questions(docs, ids, True, 32, wordings=BLIND2), equals mdllm/questions.jsonl (sha 17225d3df1bad851).
- v4 run again on it matches all 50 published answers (0 mismatches) and scores 0.586.

verdict.corrected_impact: No published number changes, and no rule verdict changes (rules 1-3 still not met, 4-5 still met). Only the wording of the conclusion is affected. A reader free to map each kind to any of v4's three training wordings reaches 0.692, which would just meet rule 1 (0.106 against 0.10). That choice of wording was made after seeing the test set, and the margin is 0.006. The ceiling comes mostly from what the training set covers: 9 of the 20 link questions (pr_issue-due_date 4, issue_pr_author 5) score 0 under every training wording. The training set has no pr_issue due-date question and only 2 issue_pr_author questions.

verified.title: Compare questions are at chance for v4 and v7: none of their test answers comes from reading both issues' due dates
verified.evidence: On mdllm (and mdllmchanged), 0 of 8 v4 and v7 compare answers come from the plan 'A + B → due_date → earliest'. The 4 correct ones (047, 050, 051, 054) read created_at or hop to other issues (for example '... → parent_issue → referenced_by → created_at → earliest'). v8 gets 5 right, of which 2 use the proper plan. On the same 50 questions, v4's compare score across the 13 wording lists ranges from 2 to 6 out of 8. Even on training, 4 of v4's 8 correct compare answers come from improper plans. measure() weights the 8 compare questions as one third of the mean, so each one moves the mean by 0.042.
verified.impact: v8 − v4 = +0.015 and v7 − v4 = −0.013 are both smaller than one compare coin flip. The 0.635, 0.692 and 0.718 wording 'ceilings' each move by ±0.042 per flip. No rule changes, but no difference of 0.04 or less between arms means anything here.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not: every count holds. But it is a caveat about how to read the results, not a bug in the code. All checks were read-only. The sqlite was opened read-only, plans.answer ran in memory, and it reproduces the published v4 answers with 0 mismatches.

1. Plans on mdllm and mdllmchanged. Of the 8 compare_two answers from v4 and from v7, 0 use the plan 'A + B → due_date → earliest'. The 4 correct ones are 047, 050, 051 and 054. 047 and 051 read 'A + B → created_at → earliest'. 050 reads 'sub_issues → referenced_by → created_at → earliest'. 054 reads 'parent_issue → referenced_by → created_at → earliest'. v7's compare answers and plans are identical to v4's. v8 gets 5 of 8 right, and 2 of those (047, 051) use the proper plan. On mdtrain, v4, v7 and v8 each get 8 of 8, but only 4 use the proper plan (042, 044, 045, 047). 041, 043, 046 and 048 do not; 041 even uses '→ due_date → latest'.

2. Weighting. All 8 compare questions are compare_two. measure() takes the mean of the three groups (factbank_multi.py:538, `groups = ("link", "combine", "compare")`). So one compare question moves the mean by 1/8/3 = 0.0417. One link question moves it by 0.0167 and one combine question by 0.0152. The pre-registration specifies this weighting, so line 538 is correct as written.

3. Wording spread. I rebuilt the test set with questions(docs, mdllm dsids, True, 32, wordings=…) for each of the 13 single wordings. Every one yields the same 50 ids, expected answers and gold documents, and the published BLIND2 set reproduces exactly. v4's compare score runs from 2 of 8 (retest wording 2) to 6 of 8 (blind wording 2). The standard wording (training wording 1) gives 0.635 with compare at 4 of 8, and only 2 of those come from the proper plan. blind wording 2 gives v4 0.718, which is at or above 0.686, mostly through compare luck: 6 of 8, none from the proper plan.

So the reported facts and arithmetic are correct.
verdict.corrected_impact:
No published number or rule changes. The three-group mean is implemented as pre-registered, and every published score is reproducible.

The finding limits how the numbers can be read:
- v8 − v4 = +0.015 and v7 − v4 = −0.013 are each smaller than one compare question (0.042) and about one link or combine question.
- v4's and v7's compare score of 0.500 comes entirely from plans that never read both due dates.

It also weakens the claim being checked, that "no English reader in front of v4 could reach 0.686". The 0.635 standard-wording figure contains 2 compare answers that are right without using the due-date plan. Other single wordings move v4's compare score from 2 to 6 of 8, a swing of ±0.083 on the mean from compare alone. One wording, blind wording 2, already puts v4 at 0.718. The rule outcomes (1 and 2 not met by margins of about 0.09–0.11; 3 not met; 4 and 5 met) do not change.

One correction to the title: on the test set v4 can read both due dates. With the standard wording it uses the proper plan on 2 of 8 compare questions. It does so on 0 of 8 only under the published BLIND2 wording.

verified.title: Hub cluster ENG-4821/ENG-4822/ENG-4832, all 'Done': every link gain v7 and v8 show over v4 comes from it, and v7's come from reading the wrong ticket
verified.evidence: ENG-4821 is in the gold docs of 6 of the 20 link questions. It is the target of 5 (022, 026, 028, 041, 042) and the source of 1 (031), so 'target of 6' is slightly off. It also appears in compare_two-053. Two of those questions have the same answer (026 and 042: due 2026-02-21) and three have the same answer 'Done' (022, 028, 041). ENG-4821, ENG-4822 and ENG-4832 link to each other and are 3 of the only 4 'Done' tickets among 34. v7 and v8 beat v4 on link only on 022 and 028. The journals show v7 reads ENG-4822's status: in 022 by two dependencies hops to [ENG-4822, ENG-4826]; in 028 by walking back to ENG-4822 itself. Both score only because ENG-4822 is also 'Done'. ticket_link-status-034 is scored right for every arm, but v4 and v7 read ENG-4832's own status via PR #663 and v8 reads ENG-4821. Separately, ticket_link-status-025 is right for all arms because it reads the creator's issues (both 'In Progress', the most common value), not ENG-21456.
verified.impact: v7's link score of 0.40 drops to 0.30 if answers taken from the wrong ticket are not credited (mean 0.539 instead of 0.573). v8's +0.10 link gain rests on two questions about one document with the same answer, which is effectively one independent item. No rule outcome changes, but there is no support for 'the reader or glossary helps with linking'.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute each claim and every one held up when I re-ran the checks myself.

**Where the gains are.** I re-scored the 20 link questions with own_score against scratchpad/mdllm/factbank_{v4,v7,v8}.jsonl:
- v4 gets 7 right (0.35): 015, 017, 025, 027, 034, 041, 045.
- v7 gets 8 right (0.40). It gains 022 and 028 and loses 027.
- v8 gets 9 right (0.45). It gains 022 and 028.
- So 022 and 028 are the only link questions where v7 or v8 beats v4. Both have gold answer ENG-4821, value 'Done'.

**Why v7 gets them.** The answer is read from the entities reached on the last hop (plans.py execute, lines 181-206: `ents = self.follow(...)`, then the field values of those ents). The journals show:
- **022 (v7):** the path is DES-15830 → dependencies → dependencies. Hop 1 reaches ENG-4821 and PM-221. Hop 2 reaches only the ENG-4822 document (dsid_...31354b) and key:eng-4826, which has no document and no status. So 'Done' comes from ENG-4822.
- **028 (v7):** the path is ENG-4822 → referenced_by → dependencies. Hop 2 reaches the ENG-4822 document itself, plus key:eng-4823 and key:eng-4826. So v7 reads the status of the ticket the question asks about, not the linked one.
- In both, v7's rewrite was used (used_rewrite = True). It only fixed the field ("state" became "status"; v4 had answered with ENG-4822's assignee, Benji Okafor). The hop count stayed wrong.
- **v8** in both questions ends on ENG-4821 together with ENG-4832, both 'Done', so its answers do include the correct ticket.

**How lucky 'Done' is.** I queried factbank.sqlite and factbank_v2.sqlite read-only. Of the 34 tickets that have a status, 4 are 'Done': ENG-18426, ENG-4821, ENG-4822 and ENG-4832. The three ENG-48xx tickets link to each other, as the hops above show.

**The other wrong-ticket answers.**
- **034** (gold answer is ENG-4822's status): v4 and v7 go ENG-4832 → PR #663 → linked_linear and read ENG-4832's own status. v8 goes dependencies → dependencies and reads ENG-4821.
- **025:** all three arms go creator (Priya Patel) → assignee_of and read her two tickets, ENG-88712 and PM-24001, both 'In Progress'. None of them reads ENG-21456.

**The pre-registration line.** ENG-4821 (dsid_...7cdd4b) is in the gold documents of 6 link questions, but as the target of only 5 (022, 026, 028, 041, 042). In 031 it is the source and ENG-4822 is the target. It is also in compare_two-053. So line 78's "target of 6" is slightly wrong.

**Same results on the changed copy.** The mdllmchanged set gives the same per-question pattern.

**The impact needs correcting.** The reviewer's figures (v7 link 0.30, mean 0.539) withhold credit for wrong-ticket answers from v7 only. That arithmetic is right but one-sided, because 025 and 034 are also wrong-ticket answers, for every arm.
verdict.corrected_impact:
The published numbers are computed correctly under the pre-registered measure (exact match), so no number is wrong and no rule changes.

If answers read from the wrong ticket get no credit, the rule has to apply to every arm, not just v7. Then:
- **v4:** loses 025 and 034. Link 0.25, mean 0.553.
- **v7:** loses 022, 028, 025 and 034. Link 0.20, mean 0.506.
- **v8:** loses 025 and 034. Link 0.35, mean 0.567.

So v7 minus v4 is -0.047 and v8 minus v4 is +0.014. Rules 1 and 2 stay not met. Rule 3 is still failed by both arms, since their training scores are 0.927 or higher. Rules 4 and 5 are unaffected.

What does change is how the results should be read:
- v7's +0.05 link gain over v4 is not genuine. Both of its gained answers come from reading ENG-4822, which happens to share ENG-4821's 'Done'.
- v8's +0.10 link gain rests on two questions with the same answer about one hub document. In both, v8 also reads ENG-4832, which is 'Done' as well, so a single answer came out partly by luck.
- So neither arm shows evidence that it helps with linking.
- One wording fix belongs in docs/FACTBANK_LLM_PREREGISTRATION.md:78 or the results write-up: the document is in 6 link questions, as the target of 5 and the source of 1.

verified.title: The training split has no PR → issue due-date question, but the test has 4, and v7's menu offers that standard question anyway
verified.evidence: mdtrain has pr_issue with fields assignee 2, status 2, due_date 0, and issue_pr_author 2. mdllm has pr_issue due_date 4, status 3, assignee 1, and issue_pr_author 5. The field is drawn at random at line 292. With v4 weights, all 4 due-date questions score 0 under every one of the 13 wording lists. Even 'When is the Linear issue linked from PR #N due?' (menu item 2, which v7 produced verbatim for 020, 026, 037 and 042) gets the assignee: the top plan is linked_linear → assignee (0.985), and the right plan ranks 8th to 20th (0.83–0.85).
verified.impact: 4 of 20 link questions (0.067 of every arm's mean) cannot be reached by any reader. This also widens rule 3's test-vs-training gap, which compares against a training set with no such questions. Without these 4, v7 on the test set would score about 0.606, still far below 0.816, so rule 3 stays not met. It should be reported as a gap in the training split, not as a failure to read English.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. Every factual claim checks out.

1) Counts, from questions.jsonl. mdtrain (48 questions) has pr_issue assignee 2, status 2, due_date 0, and issue_pr_author 2. mdllm and mdllmchanged (50 each) have pr_issue due_date 4, status 3, assignee 1, and issue_pr_author 5. The field is drawn at random per unit at src/cie/eval/factbank_multi.py:292 (`field = rng.choice([f for f in ("assignee", "due_date", "status") if iss["raw"].get(f)] ...)`). split() caps units per kind, not per field. So nothing guarantees that the training split contains a PR → issue due-date question, and it contains none.

2) Published scores. In llm_report.json, pr_issue-due_date-020, 026, 037 and 042 score 0 for v1, v4, v6, v7 and v8 on both the test set and the changed copy. v4 and v7 answer an assignee name; v8 answers a status.

3) v7's rewrites. For all four, the `read` rows show used_rewrite=true with the exact menu item 2 ("When is the Linear issue linked from PR #N due?"). The plan is still `linked_linear [linear] → assignee → single`.

4) Reproduction. I ran plans.answer read-only (sqlite opened with mode=ro, no files written) on the mdllm bank with mdtrain/plan_lessons_v4.json and fb50/lessons.json. I tried all 13 pr_issue due_date wordings: T training 3, T held-out 2, RETEST 2, NEW_WORDS 2, BLIND 2, BLIND2 2. All 52 question-wording pairs score 0. For the standard wording, the top plan is linked_linear → assignee at 0.984–0.985. The correct plan, linked_linear → due_date → single, ranks 9th, 16th, 21st and 19th (1-indexed, so 8–20 counting from zero) at 0.834–0.847.

I also tried 9 more direct phrasings with v4 weights and 10 with v8 weights, such as "What is the due date of the Linear issue linked from PR #N?" and "#N due date". All scored 0 out of 4. So "no reader can reach them" holds in practice for these weights.

The same pattern appears in every earlier set. Due-date questions on this kind score 0 for v4, v7 and v8 in mdfresh (3), mdwords (2) and mdblind (1). FACTBANK_MULTI_RESULTS.md blames this on "words never seen in training". The cause is broader: no training question of this kind asks for this field.

5) Impact arithmetic is correct. The link group has 20 questions, so 4/20 = 0.2 of link, which is 0.067 of the three-group mean for every arm. With the four removed, the test set gives v4 0.615, v7 0.606 and v8 0.638.

This is a real defect in how the training split was built: the field is not stratified, so a test question type has no training counterpart. The pre-registration lists "pull request → Linear issue: 8" without disclosing this. It changes the interpretation, but no published number is miscomputed and no rule decision flips.
verdict.corrected_impact:
The published numbers are computed correctly under the pre-registered rules and do not change. Re-scoring without the four PR → issue due-date questions, which score 0 in every arm and on both sets, gives the following.

Test set:
- v4 0.586 → 0.615
- v7 0.573 → 0.606
- v8 0.601 → 0.638

Changed copy:
- v7 0.558 → 0.591
- v8 0.601 → 0.638

Rule by rule:
- Rule 1: v7 − v4 goes from −0.013 to −0.009. Still not met.
- Rule 2: v8 − v4 goes from +0.015 to +0.023. Still not met.
- Rule 3: v7 0.606 against 0.816 and v8 0.638 against 0.836. Still not met; the gap narrows by about 0.033–0.037.
- Rule 4: still met.
- Rule 5: training is unaffected.

The correction is to the write-up. 4 of the 20 link questions (0.067 of each arm's mean) ask for a field that the training split never pairs with this kind (mdtrain has 0 such questions). With v4's weights, no wording reaches the right plan, including the standard one v7 produced verbatim. Those 4 misses come from a gap in the training split, not from failing to read English. That also explains part of the ceiling in the "standard wording gives v4 0.635" argument.

verified.title: Reader does not strip the menu number the numbered prompt invites ('10. ...'). This changes the 'right standard question' count from 15 to 13
verified.evidence: _ask only does .strip().strip('"').strip(). The model echoes the menu number in rewrites that start with '10. '. Counts: 3 cache rows in reader_mdllm, 3 in mdllmchanged, 3 in mdtrain, 7 in mdfresh, 5 in mdwords, 10 in mdblind. Of these, 2 used rewrites on the test set (action_owner_issues-036 and -040) are otherwise exactly the standard question. Re-answering all 11 used numbered rewrites across the sets with and without the prefix gives the same score every time. On the test set, an exact string match against the standard question gives 13 of 50 (all among the 31 used); ignoring the '10. ' prefix gives 15. Both the 31 and the 13 in the claim are correct as strict counts.
verified.impact: No answer or score changes. The reported 'how often the rewrite was the right standard question' is 13 under strict matching and 15 if the menu number is treated as noise. Whichever is published should say which matching it used.

verdict.reason:
The reviewer's facts are right, but they don't show a defect in any published number. I checked each part.

(1) Code: src/cie/factbank/reader.py:77 does only `.strip().strip('"').strip()`. The numbered menu is built at reader.py:42, and item 10 is action_owner_issues. Counts of rewrites starting with '<n>. ' in scratchpad/llm/reader_*.jsonl: mdllm 3, mdllmchanged 3, mdtrain 3, mdfresh 7, mdwords 5, mdblind 10. These match the reviewer's.

(2) Test set: I rebuilt the standard-wording questions with factbank_multi.questions(docs, dsids, True, 32, wordings={k: [v[0][0]]}). All 50 ids match the test questions, and all 50 expected answers are equal. Used rewrites: 31. Exact match with the standard question: 13, all among the 31 used. With the leading '\d+\.\s+' removed: 15. The extra two are action_owner_issues-036 and -040. Each is '10. ' followed by the exact standard question. action_owner_issues-033 is also numbered but was not used.

(3) Effect on answers: across all sets, 11 numbered rewrites were actually used (2 in mdllm, 2 in mdllmchanged, 7 in mdblind). I re-ran them in memory with plans.answer and the v4 plan lessons, with and without the prefix. All 11 published answers reproduce. Removing the prefix changes 0 answers and 0 own_score values. reader.keeps checks substrings, so the prefix cannot change whether a rewrite is used: the 31 stays 31.

So no score or rule result changes. The claim being checked says '13 exactly the standard question'. That is a strict count and it states its own matching rule, so it is correct as published. The only thing left is a wording question: the pre-registration (docs/FACTBANK_LLM_PREREGISTRATION.md:115) asks to report 'how often the rewrite was the right standard question'. That reads more loosely, so 15 or more could be argued. This is a matter of how the number is described, not a defect in the code or the results. Not stripping the menu number is a harmless robustness gap; here it had no effect.

Housekeeping: a mistyped shell redirect briefly created an empty file, chk_prefix.py, in the session folder, the parent of the scratchpad and outside the repository. I deleted it right away. Nothing in the repository or the scratch folder was changed.
verdict.corrected_impact: No answer, score or rule result changes. The 11 used numbered rewrites give identical answers with and without the prefix, and the used-rewrite count stays 31 of 50. On the test set, 13 of 50 rewrites exactly match the standard question; with the leading menu number removed, 15 do. The published '13 exactly the standard question' is accurate as worded. Calling it 'the right standard question' (the pre-registered item) should say exact matching was used. Optional: also give 15, with the menu number treated as noise.

unverified.title: Reader cache is keyed on the question text alone. Model and prompt are never checked, so stale rewrites would be reused silently
unverified.evidence: __init__ loads rows keyed by r['question'] (lines 65-69). read() calls the model only when the question is missing from the cache. The stored 'model' field is never compared, and no prompt hash is stored. system_prompt() is built at runtime from factbank_multi.T, so any edit to T or to the prompt text would replay old rewrites under the new configuration. This did not happen here: the current system_prompt() has sha256 7ac2eb466f0737bef3f3..., matching the pre-registration's 7ac2eb466f0737be. ollama_serve_now.log shows 300 /api/chat calls: 2 probe calls at 03:51 (rw_probe.json, a different prompt and a question outside the test set) and 298 between 03:58 and 04:11. That equals the 298 rows across the six reader_*.jsonl files, with no duplicates. Re-running v7 from the caches with current code reproduces every published v7 answer on mdllm, mdllmchanged and mdtrain.
unverified.impact: No effect on published numbers. It is a risk to reproducibility if the test is rerun after any change to the menu or prompt.

unverified.title: The glossary's 'creator' target adds 'created' (stem 'creat'), which matches the created_at date field rather than creator. Several standard words are not from the training wordings
unverified.evidence: tokens_of('creator') = {'creator'} but tokens_of('created_at') = {'creat'}, and words(CANON['creator']) = {'creat'}. So a 'creator' glossary phrase raises field_overlap for created_at (a date) and not for the creator field. The pre-registration says the standard words come from the training questions' own wordings, but no training wording contains 'created', 'reviewers' or 'latest'. Counting matched targets over mdllm, mdllmchanged and mdtrain finds no hit for the creator, reviewers or latest targets. The other mappings were checked and behave: training and answering use the same stemmer and the same glossary words, and learn_plans retrained in memory reproduces plan_lessons_v4.json and plan_lessons_v8.json exactly (weights, rel/agg/kind assoc). No glossary phrase matched inside a person name, key or PR number in any of the six sets.
unverified.impact: No question in the scored sets triggers it, so v8's 0.601, 0.986 and 0.601 do not change. It would mis-target any future question that uses a 'creator' phrase.

unverified.title: Action items: duplicated answers, right answers by coincidence, the customer-attendee name collision, and a v8 collapse that has nothing to do with English
unverified.evidence: The 8 action-item questions have only 5 distinct answers. 019, 029 and 030 all expect [ENG-88712, PM-24001] (owner Priya Patel). 023 and 024 share [ENG-44277, ENG-54821, PM-14230]. v4 and v7 get 029 and 030 right through meeting → redwood_attendees → assignee_of over [Jordan Lee, Priya Patel], which works only because Jordan Lee has no Linear issue in the set. The owner of 036 is the customer's CISO, Priya Desai. Line 237 joins owners to assignees by name alone, so the expected answer is an employee's issues. The changed copy renames both people to 'Anouk Ashdown', so the collision is still there. Every arm scores 036 as 1. Without it: v4 0.585, v7 0.570 (changed copy 0.554), v8 0.596; no rule changes. v8 scores 0.25 on action items in the test (0.875 in training) because it starts from a different action item in the same meeting (019, 024, 033, 040) or takes owner → creator_of → assignee (029, 030). It still scores 0.25 with the standard training wording. v8's fanout weight flipped from +0.23 (v4) to −1.00.
unverified.impact: Each shared owner counts 2 to 3 times in combine. v8's combine loss (−0.18), which is what sinks rule 2, comes from re-learned planner weights, not from the glossary's English. v4's combine score of 0.909 includes 2 coincidental answers. No rule outcome changes.

unverified.title: '13 exactly the standard question' is true, but it is not the preregistered 'right standard question' count: 25 of the 31 used rewrites ask the right kind
unverified.evidence: Recounted from mdllm/factbank_v7.jsonl and llm/reader_mdllm.jsonl: 31 of 50 rewrites were used, and 13 match the oracle question exactly. Those 13 are all 8 pr_issue and all 5 issue_pr_author questions. 12 more used rewrites ask the right kind without matching word for word: paraphrases for count, first-due and 'points to', the right template with a key in the PR slot ('pull request #ENG-27651'), and '10. ' prefixes on action items. 6 ask the wrong kind: person_first-002, -008 and -012 become status questions; ticket_link-assignee-027 and -032 become PR-author questions; -031 becomes a PR-assignee question. All 8 compare rewrites were rejected because they dropped keys. The 13 exact rewrites gain nothing: v4 already answers the same 4 correctly from the original wording, and the other 9 (due-date and author) fail under the standard wording too. On the other copies: 29 of 50 used (changed), 35 of 48 used (training).
unverified.impact: This changes only a reported-only statistic. Depending on the definition it is 13/31 (exact) or 25/31 (right kind), and the write-up should say which. No rule changes.

unverified.title: Rule 4 cannot fail for v4 or v8 by construction. For v7, renaming alone flips 8 rewrite decisions
unverified.evidence: mdllmchanged has the same 50 ids. Only 14 question texts change (7 person_count, 7 person_first), and 13 expected values change (person-valued answers). v4 and v8 score exactly the same on both copies, per question. For v7, renaming flips use_rewrite on 8 questions (person_count-001/003/005/007, person_first-004/006/010/014) but changes only one score (person_first-008, 1 → 0). That gives 0.573 → 0.558.
unverified.impact: Rule 4 being 'met' tells us something only about v7, and v7's margin (−0.015 against −0.05) is a single question. No published number is wrong.
